title: Clinical trial: the effects of emulsifiers in the food supply on disease activity in Crohn's disease: an exploratory double-blinded randomised feeding trial
authors: Fitzpatrick JA, Gibson PR, Taylor KM, Anderson EJ, Friedman AB, Ardalan ZS, et al.
population: Adults with symptomatic, sonographically active Crohn's disease with ileal involvement on at least 2 months of stable medical therapy
funder: This work was supported by JAF receiving the Crohn's and Colitis Australia PhD Scholarship. EPH was supported through research grants from the National Health & Medical Research Council Investigator Grant and Crohn's and Colitis Foundation Litwin Pioneers Program. The study was supported by a grant from the Eva and Tom Breuer Foundation.
authorConflicts: Several authors declared honoraria, consultancies, shareholdings or grants from companies including Mindset Health, PepsiCo, Atmo Biosciences, Dr Falk Pharma, AbbVie, Janssen and Takeda.
result: High-emulsifier versus low-emulsifier diet, both following Australian healthy eating guidelines, with all food provided. Clinical remission (Harvey-Bradshaw Index below 5) in 9 of 12 versus 7 of 12 (P = 0.67); IBUS-SAS fell on both diets; faecal calprotectin did not change; no outcome differed between diets.
